newsitem.title: UK: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - July 29.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - July 29.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST.....
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

PARIS - French pay television group Canal Plus says it is suing the French terrestrial television channels and their media-selling units over their refusal to accept an advert promoting Canal Plus last April.

FRANKFURT - Advertising income at private German television stations has a solid potential for growth to the year 2000, bank analysts say. Ad income at private channels could increase five percent every year until the end of the millennium, analysts from the DG Bank say in a report.

LONDON - Scotland, the home of scotch whisky, is to be a test market for tequila, which drinks group Allied Domecq hopes to popularise in Britain. Allied Domecq says it will launch its new Sauza Conmemorativo brand, a premium version of its existing Sauza tequila, in Scotland on August 4 with a 1.5 million pound ($2.4 million) advertising and marketing campaign carrying the theme "Reawaken your senses".

CHICAGO - Midas International Corp, the world's largest franchised automotive service operation, says it named two Chicago agencies as finalists in its search for a new advertising agency for its $25 million national account. DDB Needham and Foote, Cone & Belding will make creative presentations to Midas in mid-August.

LONDON - Advertising agencies are facing increasing competition from management consultancies that are muscling in on their turf by providing clients with strategic branding and communications advice, industry experts say.

BONN - German telecommunications group Deutsche Telekom declares an advertising victory at the Tour de France, where the team it sponsored not only won the race but invaluable worldwide publicity. Telekom spokesman Ulrich Lissek says Telekom's brand-name recognition reached about 96 percent in Germany through its sponsorship of the cyclists.
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

MADRID - Antonio Asensio resigns as chairman of Spain's Antena 3, the television station says in a statement. Six other board members also resigned after Spanish telecoms provider Telefonica announced a deal to buy 25 percent of Antena 3 and a controlling stake in its GMA subsidiary, which has lucrative rights to broadcast soccer matches.

SAN FRANCISCO - WebTV Networks Inc chief executive officer Steve Perlman says the company expects to reach 250,000 subscribers by the end of 1997, more than double its current 115,000 users. WebTV offers Internet access via television sets.

NEW YORK - America Online Inc, the Internet provider with the largest subscriber pool, raises the bar for many of the eletronic retailers doing business via its service. Starting next month retailers that had paid commissions to AOL for the right to peddle their wares on its Market Place service will pay a flat fee.

ROME - Major television broadcasters and media groups operating within Italy say they have reached a preliminary deal to create a single digital television platform. The accord involves communications group Mediaset, state broadcaster RAI, state-controlled telecoms group Telecom Italia, French broadcaster Canal Plus and its majority owned pay-tv, Telepiu, as well as Cecchi Gori Communications.

NEW YORK - News Corp Ltd says the U.S. Department of Justice probe into its proposed acquisition of Heritage Media Corp is focused on the coupon operations of both companies. News Corp operates a busines that provides merchandise coupons in newspapers, as well as a smaller business that provides coupons found in grocery stores.

EMMAUS, Pennsylvania - Rodale Press has agreed to acquire New Woman magazine from K-III Communications Corp, the companies say. New Woman's circulation of one million and advertising base of 1,000 pages create a perfect synergy with other Rodale publications such as Men's Health and Prevention, the companies say.
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

LONDON - Hamburger chain Burger King, owned by Britain's Grand Metropolitan Plc, says it plans to withdraw from France after a review of its operations in Europe. Burger King has a total 39 restaurants in France, mainly in and around Paris.

TOKYO - Strong beer sales put the fizz in Asahi Breweries Ltd's earnings in the first half of the year while its rival, Kirin Brewery Co Ltd, came up short. Asahi reports parent current profit rose 44.9 percent in the first six months to 18.17 billion yen ($154.7 million). Kirin's parent current profit declined to 25.25 billion yen from 27.53 billion yen a year ago.

SANTA CLARA, California - Intel Corp. and Advanced Micro Devices Inc. slash prices on their best-selling computer chips, stepping up their ongoing battle for market share. Intel, the world's largest maker of computer chips, cut prices on its popular Pentium chips up to 57 percent, prompting Advanced Micro to trim prices on its new K6 chip by as much as 55 percent.
DETROIT - Ford Motor Co. will introduce a smaller replacement for the mid-sized Mercury Cougar coupe now being phased out. A national advertising campaign is planned for the autumn.
LONDON - Branding has become the most important factor in the marketing of UK financial services, according to a report by market research group Datamonitor.

TOKYO - Shiseido Co Ltd is planning to launch new products targeted solely at the international market, in an attempt to be one of the world's top three cosmetics firms by 2005, says director Yasutaka Mori. Shiseido on September 1 will launch a new skincare and makeup brand called "Za".
CONSUMER TRENDS:

NICOSIA - After years in decline, the used car market in Cyprus is booming. In three years, the industry has turned into a goldmine for dealers importing second hand vehicles from Japan, after parliament amended a law allowing imports of cars up to five years old from two years previously.

SYDNEY - Australian researchers who have extracted a special powder from cows' milk which could heal wounds and smooth wrinkles, believe the discovery is worth up to A$20 ($14.73) billion worldwide. Marketing negotiations are already underway with a number of major international cosmetics and wound care companies and manufacturing rights have been awarded.
